hallucinations.claim: Recent studies have demonstrated that general-purpose language models exhibit suboptimal performance on legal documents due to significant lexical and structural disparities between these models and domain-specific content (Jayakumar et al., 2023).
hallucinations.issue: The ground truth states that 'general-purpose language models perform poorly on legal texts due to domain-specific terminology and structural differences,' but it does not specify that this is due to 'significant lexical and structural disparities' or attribute this directly to 'recent studies' in the way the claim frames it. hallucinations.claim: Furthermore, training data limitations restrict the applicability of legal information retrieval and question answering systems to broader legal domains (Pham et al., 2024).
